summary_ja: プロジェクト・ファイナンス、オブジェクト・ファイナンス、コモディティ・ファイナンス（特定貸付債権）のリスク・ウェイトを個別格付に応じて定め、無格付の場合の区分ごとの値（運用段階前百三十パーセント等）と、要件を満たす運用段階のプロジェクト・ファイナンスの八十パーセントを定める。
summary_en: Specialized lending (project, object and commodity finance) is weighted by its issue-specific rating; unrated exposures take 100% (130% for pre-operational project finance), and high-quality operational project finance meeting ten conditions may take 80%.

terms.ja: 特定貸付債権向けエクスポージャー
プロジェクト・ファイナンス向けエクスポージャー
コモディティ・ファイナンス向けエクスポージャー

paragraphs: Notwithstanding the provisions of the preceding Article, the risk weight of exposures to corporates, etc. for the businesses listed in the following items (referred to as "exposures to specialized lending" in this Article and in paragraph (1) of the following Article) shall be as set out in the left column of the table of paragraph (1) of the preceding Article, according to the credit risk category corresponding to the issue-specific rating assigned to the exposure to specialized lending. In this case, where the obligor of the exposure to specialized lending has an issuer rating, that issuer rating shall not be used in determining the risk weight. (i) Credit extended to a specific project, such as a power plant, chemical plant, mining project, transport infrastructure, environmental infrastructure or telecommunications infrastructure, where the source of interest payments and repayment is limited mainly to the revenue from that project, and the lender, through the terms of the credit, has a substantial degree of control over the tangible assets of the project and the income from them (referred to as "project finance exposures" in paragraph (3), items (iii) and (iv) and in paragraph (4)). (ii) Credit extended for the acquisition of ships, aircraft, satellites, railways, vehicles or other tangible assets, where the source of interest payments and repayment is limited mainly to the income from those tangible assets, the tangible assets are pledged as collateral, and the lender, through the terms of the credit, has a substantial degree of control over the tangible assets and the income from them. (iii) Short-term credit extended to finance reserves, inventories or receivables of commodities listed on a commodity exchange, such as crude oil, metals or grains, where the source of interest payments and repayment is limited mainly to the proceeds from selling those listed commodities, and the lender, through the terms of the credit, has a substantial degree of control over the listed commodities and the income from them (referred to as "commodity finance exposures" in paragraph (3), item (ii)).

Where, as a result of the due diligence analysis of an exposure to specialized lending, the credit standing of the business relating to that exposure is assessed as carrying higher risk than the credit standing indicated by the credit risk category corresponding to the issue-specific rating, the risk weight corresponding to a credit risk category one or more grades lower than the credit risk category corresponding to that issue-specific rating shall be used; provided, however, that a risk weight corresponding to a credit risk category higher than the credit risk category corresponding to that issue-specific rating shall not be used.

Where an exposure to specialized lending is unrated, the risk weight specified in each of the following items shall be applied according to the category of exposure listed in that item. (i) Object finance exposures: 100%. (ii) Commodity finance exposures: 100%. (iii) Project finance exposures before the operational phase: 130%. (iv) Project finance exposures in the operational phase: 100%.

Notwithstanding the provisions of item (iv) of the preceding paragraph, an Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the standardized approach may set at 80% the risk weight of project finance exposures in the operational phase that satisfy all of the following requirements. (i) That the obligor of the project finance exposure has the capacity to meet its monetary obligations in accordance with the repayment schedule. (ii) That the Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the standardized approach has judged that the capacity provided in the preceding item is not easily affected by the business cycle or changes in the business environment. (iii) That the obligor is restricted from acting to the detriment of the Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the standardized approach. (iv) That sufficient financial arrangements have been made to cover contingent expenditures and meet working capital requirements in the business relating to the project finance exposure. (v) That any of the following requirements is satisfied: (a) That a contract satisfying all of the following requirements has been concluded with the offtaker (meaning the purchaser of the goods, services, etc. that are the object of the business relating to the project finance exposure; the same applies hereinafter in this paragraph). (1) Where construction of the facilities, etc. used in the business has been completed, the offtaker pays stable and sufficient amounts to cover the operating costs, repair costs, debt service costs and dividends required to run the business. (2) Except where the facilities, etc. used in the business lack the predetermined performance or cannot be used, the amount paid is not affected by demand for the goods, services, etc. that are the object of the business and is not reduced. (b) That the revenue of the business relating to the project finance exposure is subject to rate-of-return regulation in the jurisdiction in which the business is carried out (meaning regulation under which the regulatory authority of that jurisdiction sets the rate of profit, etc. it considers appropriate for the business). (c) That a take-or-pay contract (meaning a contract under which the offtaker undertakes to pay the obligor a fixed amount as consideration under set conditions, whether or not it receives the goods, services, etc. that are the object of the business) has been concluded with the offtaker for the revenue of the business relating to the project finance exposure. (vi) That the source of interest payments and repayment of the project finance exposure depends mainly on revenue from creditworthy offtakers (meaning offtakers that are central governments, central banks, the Bank for International Settlements, the International Monetary Fund, the European Central Bank, the European Union, the European Stability Mechanism, the European Financial Stability Facility, multilateral development banks, local governments in Japan, the Japan Finance Organization for Municipalities, land development public corporations, local housing supply public corporations, local road public corporations, Japanese government-affiliated agencies, public sector entities other than foreign central governments and central banks, or corporates, etc. (limited to those to which a risk weight of 80% or less applies under the provisions of the preceding Article); the same applies in item (viii)). (vii) That the contract for the credit relating to the project finance exposure contains provisions for effective protection of creditors in the event of default. (viii) That, where a creditworthy offtaker terminates a contract relating to the business of the project finance exposure, the creditworthy offtaker is expected to take the measures necessary to prevent a loss to that business. (ix) That the assets necessary to operate the business relating to the project finance exposure and the contractual rights held by the obligor of the project finance exposure have been pledged as collateral to the extent permitted under the laws and regulations (including foreign laws and regulations) applicable to the business. (x) That, in the event of default, the creditors (including the Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the standardized approach) can take control of the business relating to the project finance exposure.

The "operational phase" in paragraph (3), items (iii) and (iv) and in the preceding paragraph means the phase in which the entity operating the project satisfies all of the following requirements. (i) That it has positive net cash flow sufficient to cover its remaining contractual obligations. (ii) That its long-term debt is declining.
